info.name: LLM Chat
info.summary: Chat with LLMs directly from your browser — the server never sees your prompts
info.description:
**Privacy-first by architecture. Batteries included. Bring your own LLM.**
A chat interface for large language models where **your browser talks directly to the LLM backend**. Nextcloud acts only as configuration storage and archive target — it is never a proxy and never sees prompts or responses. Not "we promise not to look": it structurally cannot.
Because the requests originate in the browser, `localhost` resolves from the *user's* machine. Your Nextcloud can live in a datacenter and still talk to an Ollama instance running on your laptop — no tunnel, no VPN, no exposed port. No server-side LLM app can do that.
Features:
* Bring your own backend: Ollama, llama.cpp, LiteLLM, OpenRouter, vLLM — anything OpenAI-compatible * Multiple connections with encrypted API key storage, multiple profiles per connection * Profiles carry model, system prompt, temperature, token budget, streaming and reasoning switches * Streaming responses with a stop button, edit-and-retry, regenerate * Optional agent tools: web search via your own SearXNG, page fetching, clock, and read-only access to your own Nextcloud (Unified Search and Collectives) — no MCP server, no extra container, no app password needed * Approval dialog before any tool call that leaves the browser, on by default * Chat history in IndexedDB — local to the browser, by design * Archive chats as Markdown files into your Nextcloud files * Profile export/import as JSON (never contains secrets)
**Note:** API keys are stored encrypted on the server but are necessarily delivered to the browser, since that is where the request is made. Each user only ever sees their own key.
